set.body:
Why
The campaign closes only on broad public evidence, not on the sum of local microbenchmark victories. This child reruns the whole court after all promoted changes and makes remaining losses explicit.

Scope
- On a calm host, rerun the pinned JVM public NumPy matrix, JVM allocation court, full-linked Node court, semantic and layout signatures, all laws, fullLink, and browser correctness.
- Compare before and after distributions by operation family, dtype, size, and layout. Publish geomeans and every regression; do not hide losses in an aggregate.
- Audit dispatch conditions for benchmark names, exact fixture sizes, or other non-semantic specialization. Audit hot loops for boxing, callbacks, interpretation, and size-proportional temporary allocation.
- Record JVM-only, shared, Scala.js-specific, promoted, rejected, and deferred decisions separately.

Outcome targets
- Target JVM comparison geomean at or above 0.75 of matched NumPy and predicate geomean at or above 0.60, with a side-1024 overall geomean at or above 0.90. Treat these as campaign targets, never permission to falsify semantics or overfit cases.
- Targeted full-linked Node classes improve by their child thresholds with no unexplained established-case regression above 10 percent. Node results are relative to the pinned Node baseline, not NumPy.
- Any missed target requires a structural profile and a concrete accept, defer, or reject decision; it cannot disappear from the receipt.

Acceptance
- Exact semantic and layout parity holds for every JVM NumPy case and every shared JVM or Scala.js signature.
- JVM and Scala.js test, law, compatibility, fullLink, and browser gates pass.
- Allocation evidence confirms no new intermediate-size temporaries outside explicit results and workspaces.
- The epic summary distinguishes achieved general speedups from runtime limits and lists the next justified frontier, if any.
- All child receipts are linked and the epic can close without relying on noisy or missing evidence.
set.title: Ratify the next Ravel performance frontier across JVM and Scala.js
